subject: gk
question: Untouchability is against which of the following fundamental rights?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Right to equality**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Right to Equality is one of the six fundamental rights provided by the Constitution of India to its citizens.
 
• It includes equality before the law, prohibition of discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth.
 
• It also includes equality of opportunity in matters of public employment and the abolition of untouchability and titles.
 
• The practice of untouchability is a punishable offense under Article 17 of the Indian Constitution, which falls under the Right to Equality.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Right to Freedom of Religion**

 
 
• It is one of the fundamental rights enshrined in the Indian Constitution under Articles 25 to 28.
 
• It ensures freedom of conscience and the right to freely profess, practice, and propagate religion.
 
• The state cannot interfere in religious matters, but it can regulate or restrict any economic, financial, political, or other secular activities associated with religious practices.
 
• This right aims to maintain religious harmony and avoid conflicts among different religious groups.
 
 
 
• **Right to Constitutional Remedies**
 
 
• It is provided under Article 32 of the Indian Constitution and is considered the heart and soul of the Constitution by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar.
 
• This right allows individuals to move the Supreme Court or High Courts to seek enforcement of their fundamental rights.
 
• The courts have the power to issue writs like habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, quo warranto, and certiorari for the enforcement of these rights.
 
• This right ensures the protection and realization of fundamental rights and acts as a guardian of the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Right to Liberty**
 
 
• It is part of the Right to Freedom under Articles 19 to 22 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• This right guarantees freedom of speech and expression, assembly, association, movement, residence, and profession.
 
• It also includes protection in respect of conviction for offenses, protection of life and personal liberty, and protection against arrest and detention in certain cases.
 
• This right aims to promote individual liberty and protect citizens from arbitrary actions by the state.
